assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only 86-eighty-six:frederica-rosenfort@original-light-novels#86-frederica-rosenfort-character-reference-profile, the canonical Frederica Rosenfort character reference profile (the CMR-2 pilot profile, version 1.2, release 86-V2-V01-V14-1.0) at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the locked original-Japanese light novels, in which her active evidence begins in V02 and runs to V14, with Alter.1 as audited supplemental ordinary-life evidence and Alter.2 excluded. Row counts come only from the profile's own diagnostic scene bank (48 rows). The CMR-3 locator index, the CMR-9 promotion audit and ledger, the profile's validation report, the relationship register matrix, the ledgers L01, L02, L08 and L09, the numbered thematic Documents, the Phase-5 and Phase-8 artifacts and the Japanese EPUBs are not curated evidence on this subject, and nothing is borrowed from them. The profile's METHOD_PASS and CMR-9 verdicts and its HIGH, MODERATE, LOW and OPEN labels are inputs, not conclusions. No anime adaptation, V15+ volume, Alter.2 scene or other character's profile is included, and the evaluator inspected no primary source.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: The profile's developmental points from V02 (a former empress newly sheltered in the household of Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman), with inherited guilt and projection of Kiriya, her childhood knight, onto Shin (Shinei Nouzen)) through the V14 boundary. V03 is split at the decision left to her (p-011 ¶243-262) and the grief after it (p-011 ¶421-475); V08 at the rejected self-sacrifice argument (p-002 ¶1-76), the シンエイ naming boundary (p-005 ¶510-540) and the rescue overfunction (p-011 ¶27-28, ¶607-610); V12 at the Raiden (Raiden Shuga) conversation (p-006 ¶191-245), the self-rule confrontation with Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) (p-008 ¶257-301) and the self-care formulation (p-008 ¶457-465); V13 at her chosen disclosure (p-003 ¶34-35); and V14 at the New Imperial Court proclamation (p-009 ¶27). V04-V06, V07-V09 and V11-V12 are otherwise grouped phases, and V06 and V10 have no scene-bank row. No default state is set; one must be selected. Alter.1 rows are ordinary-life supplements without volume placement, and states after V14 are not established.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The profile gives a causal account of Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort): a genuinely childlike and genuinely formidable person whose archaizing register, social initiative, relational and political pattern-recognition and sensitivity to other people's self-disposal combine with a wish to make herself useful enough that nobody is abandoned. It says what moves her from observation to action: a loved person treating their own life as disposable, agency denied in the name of care, a rescue she can materially help, damaging silence, inherited power turning a person into a symbol, and a loved one spiraling. Its decision rule is that she has a low emotional threshold for wanting to intervene and an improving ability to ask whether intervention helps, anchored by the V02 restraint counterexample and the V08 rescue work (p-011 ¶607-610). It distinguishes care she accepts from protection that becomes authorship over her answer (V03 p-006 ¶102-171; V11 p-014 ¶126-159; V13 p-003 ¶180-199), and it predicts her mistakes: overreading (the accusation toward Annette (Annette Penrose), V04 p-006 ¶631-643), Kiriya-shaped projection onto Shin (Shinei Nouzen), self-use as a sacrifice (V08 p-002 ¶1-76), being outmaneuvered (V12 p-008 ¶257-301) and practical limits of her ability (V05 p-005 ¶648-681). Its prediction protocol requires developmental point, relation, state, authority context and whether her ability gives direct evidence. A would overclaim: the set is one derived pilot artifact that defers to L01, L02 and L09 outside it, the scene bank has 48 rows with V06 and V10 unsampled, her consent to restoration is open, and the profile rates her diagnosis of unfamiliar people as only moderately supportable. C would understate an account that says which consideration decides in each sampled class and predicts her overreach with its corrections.

The profile gives an ordered developmental account of Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort) with causes: V02 observer with inherited guilt, Kiriya-shaped diagnosis of Shin (Shinei Nouzen) and child need (p-006 ¶425-480; p-007 ¶444-472); V03 participant who owns the decision about Kiriya, her childhood knight (p-011 ¶243-262), and grieves without losing her register (p-011 ¶421-475); V04-V06 household embedding with fallible interpretation; V07-V09 political danger and self-use pressure (V08 p-002 ¶1-76), with the シンエイ naming boundary keeping Shin distinct from Kiriya (V08 p-005 ¶510-540) and shared rather than unilateral responsibility (V09 p-006 ¶119-134); V11-V12 helplessness revised into self-rule and self-care (V11 p-010 ¶265-300; V12 p-006 ¶191-245; p-008 ¶257-301, ¶457-465); V13 chosen disclosure and the group's recognition that her answer must be included (p-003 ¶34-35, ¶180-199); and V14 guide to Raiden (Raiden Shuga) who still jokes like herself (p-007 ¶275-350). It forbids regressions: treating every self-destructive soldier as another Kiriya, or praising her sacrifice after the V12 correction. C would understate located, causally ordered transitions with these controls. A is rejected: V04-V06 and V07-V09 are grouped phases, V06 and V10 have no row and V05, V07, V09 and V11 have one or two each, the profile says it is not a substitute for L01, her ageing is not located, and nothing after V14 is established.

The profile fixes the written-Japanese idiolect of Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort): first person わらわ, second person そなた, end forms ～じゃ, ～ではない, ～ぬ, ～ぞ, ～のう, ～であろ and ～かや, insult vocabulary (たわけ, 痴れ者, ばかもの, お人好しの死神め) and mock-bestowal framing, and states that the register is an identity-bearing baseline across household life, comedy, fear, grief, command and political argument, not a ceremonial mask. It gives state rules (fear shortens and repeats; anger adds imperatives, insults and gesture; grief reduces ornament; teasing amplifies mock status; political assertion lengthens argument), a rule that archaic grammar does not mean ornate syntax, and a located code-switch exception: she can deliberately perform sweeter child speech but keeps her word choice as part of herself (言葉の選び方もわらわの一部じゃ, Alter.1 part0023 ¶35-43). Address is directed: シンエイ for Shin (Shinei Nouzen), never キリ (V08 p-005 ¶510-540); キリ for Kiriya, her childhood knight, in memory; name or mock epithets such as 木端役人 for Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman), with no literal father-term claimed; 兄様, 姉様 and 兄さま for peers where the relation has become familial (V14 p-007 ¶275-293); and 鎖蛇 for Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) in V12. C would understate a located morphology, address system and state deltas with an explicit exception rule. A is rejected: there is no frequency or distribution data, the form she uses for Lena (Vladilena Milizé) is not given, few verbatim exemplars carry their own row, address toward unfamiliar adults and formal superiors is not given, and the L09 voice ledger is outside the set.

The profile treats ordinary life as central for Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort) and says what drives it: curiosity about experiences imperial childhood and war denied her, appetite (hunger lowers her patience), tactile comfort, and newly communal household life (Alter.1 part0022 ¶2-37). Located conduct runs across the corpus: very sweet coffee and Shin (Shinei Nouzen) removing the sugar pot (V02 p-004 ¶168-171), asking Raiden (Raiden Shuga) for food and watching him cook (V02 p-006 ¶269-293), sleepy disarray with the teddy bear (V02 p-007 ¶82-140), the first sea disappointing her expectation (V08 p-005 ¶1-20), the pumpkin-pie rush (V12 p-008 ¶457-465), a Christmas ornament in the military kitchen (V14 p-004 ¶316-322), and Alter.1 shopping, plush toys, carrying too many blankets and accepting care when injured (part0023-0024; part0027 ¶25-30; part0051 ¶2-5). It bounds inference: no favorite-food hierarchy beyond attested items, no skilled cooking, and the sea scene is not a general dislike. C would understate stated drivers with located conduct and a prediction for ordinary settings. A is rejected: there is no routine or frequency, the Alter.1 rows are not placed by volume, and animation, sleep and cooking items are described without their own rows.

Nine directed relations of Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort) are analyzed, including two reverse directions: Shin (Shinei Nouzen) as older-brother family whose self-disposal she monitors and whom she keeps distinct from Kiriya, her childhood knight (V02 p-008 ¶320-326; V03 p-006 ¶102-171; V08 p-005 ¶510-540); Shin toward her, practical and irreverent but leaving her the Kiriya decision (V03 p-011 ¶243-262); Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman), household-intimate and politically unawed, whom she wants stopped rather than mythologized when his violence breaks out (V13 p-006 ¶309-318, ¶417-428); Ernst toward her; Kiriya, whom she wants both to stop and not to lose; the surviving Spearhead peers, who tease, carry and stop her (V11 p-010 ¶265-300; p-014 ¶126-159); Raiden (Raiden Shuga), practical older-brother care and correction (V02 p-006 ¶269-293; V12 p-006 ¶191-245; V14 p-007 ¶275-350); Lena (Vladilena Milizé), older-sister companion and teasing target (V04 p-005 ¶312-347; V05 p-006 ¶630-641); and Vika (Viktor Idinarohk), a reciprocal pressure test (V12 p-008 ¶257-301; V13 p-003 ¶34-35). C would understate this partner-specific discrimination. A is rejected: Kurena (Kurena Kukumila), Anju (Anju Emma), Theo (Theoto Rikka), Annette (Annette Penrose) and Fido rest on one row each or none, interpretive authority toward Lena is only MODERATE, the relation with Ernst after V14 is MODERATE, and the relationship matrix and L02 are outside the set.

Private states of Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort) are located mainly through what she says and does: the admission of fear about Kiriya, her childhood knight, during a sleepless watch (V03 p-010 ¶55-149), the conflicting wish to stop and not to lose him (V03 p-011 ¶243-262, ¶421-475), fear of looking through her ability in case Kiriya appears (V08 p-005 ¶510-540), panic as the war worsens (V11 p-010 ¶265-300), and the V12 self-care formulation まずはわらわ自身を、わらわは労わってやらねば (p-008 ¶457-465). These states drive located choices: owning the Kiriya decision, the naming boundary, accepting being held back, and bounded responsibility. B would overclaim: the profile classifies none of its exemplars as narration, inner speech or dialogue, most interior states are inferred from speech, conduct and embodied cues, the V12 internalization of helplessness is described rather than located paragraph by paragraph, and V04-V07 interior is barely sampled. D would understate located admissions and a self-revision causally tied to her conduct.

The profile states the conflict style of Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort): she argues the premise, meaning who owns the choice, rather than only the conclusion (Shin (Shinei Nouzen) in V03; Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) in V12; adults planning her political safety in V13); she escalates quickly from reason to command, insult, repetition, physical intervention or tears (V03 p-006 ¶102-171; V14 p-007 ¶275-304); she overreads and can be cutting without a later apology converting it into a mistake (Annette (Annette Penrose), V04 p-006 ¶631-643); and she can revise after argument without submitting (Raiden (Raiden Shuga), V12 p-006 ¶191-245). It names the classes of moral interruption she treats as legitimate (self-disposal, appropriated agency, the violent collapse of Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman) in V13, suppressed legitimate anger in V14) and says that at her best she returns the choice to the other person. C would understate conditioned response families with located corrections. A is rejected: the Annette confrontation is one sample without resolution, conflict with formal adult authorities outside the household is barely sampled, and conflict over a restored throne has not happened by V14.

The profile gives Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort) argued positions with a failure mode: knowing people is worth later loss (V02 p-007 ¶353-379); the right to make the decision about Kiriya, her childhood knight (V03 p-011 ¶243-262); the argument that one child is a small sacrifice, rejected by Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman) and Shin (Shinei Nouzen) (V08 p-002 ¶1-76); responsibility shared as a comrade rather than spent as a sacrifice (V09 p-006 ¶119-134); conscience against being told where to look and self-rule as becoming わらわ自身の王 (V12 p-008 ¶257-301); self-care as a condition of caring for others (V12 p-008 ¶457-465); and the distinction between legitimate anger and indiscriminate revenge offered to Raiden (Raiden Shuga) (V14 p-007 ¶297-340). It predicts the recurring error of converting 'I can help' into 'therefore I should be spent' and separates it from defensible emergency use of her ability. C would understate located positions with a reasoning pattern and failure mode. A is rejected: whether she would accept or refuse restored sovereign office is explicitly not supportable, her positions are mostly about her own responsibility, and no adult political decision is modeled.

The profile treats the comedy of Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort) as diagnostic and gives its engines: status incongruity between imperial diction and child need (V02 p-005 ¶428-470; Alter.1 part0024 ¶2-37), retaliatory boasting when teased, mischievous romantic meddling (V04 p-005 ¶312-347; p-007 ¶157-177), insult play whose force depends on the relationship, and physical comedy in which her own force rebounds on her (V14 p-007 ¶275-293). It states when humor recedes (grief and fear suppress comic performance) and that a stranger using the same insults would not produce the same effect, and it locates the exact non-grandiosity test of the failed 'goddess' joke (V14 p-007 ¶340-350). C would understate functional rules with located forms and a suspension condition. A is rejected: the profile gives no stop rule for meddling beyond saying she sometimes enjoys the advantage too much, several forms rest on Alter.1 without volume placement, and household humor dominates the sample.

A dedicated canonical profile of Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort) over V02-V14 with Alter.1 supplemental, with 48 routed diagnostic rows: V02 9, V03 6, V04 4, V05 2, V07 1, V08 5, V09 2, V11 2, V12 3, V13 3, V14 5 and Alter.1 6. Thirteen rows name a Phase-5 locator (one only partially), and 35 are LOCATOR_GAP rows with exact EPUB routes. B would overclaim: this is a derived compression of a principal supporting character across thirteen volumes; V06 and V10 have no row and V05, V07, V09 and V11 one or two; and the narrower authorities that control conflicts (L01, L02, L09, Documents 04, 06, 08 and 09, and the matrix) are outside the set. D would understate dedicated, exactly routed coverage that reaches every developmental point the profile names.

For Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort) there are fourteen mischaracterization traps, twenty would-sound-wrong constraints and a ten-trait counterexample audit with dispositions: the archaizing register survives with an explicit code-switch exception; social forwardness, perceptiveness and abrasive care are narrowed; autonomy sensitivity survives only as resistance to authorship over her person; self-use survives as a developmental vulnerability rather than an endpoint. Located negatives include the V04 accusation toward Annette (Annette Penrose) as interpretation rather than fact (p-006 ¶631-643), the useless landscape description (V05 p-005 ¶648-681), Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) seeing through her cover story (V12 p-008 ¶257-301), the シンエイ boundary (V08 p-005 ¶510-540) and the deliberate code-switch (Alter.1 part0023 ¶3-57). C would understate these affirmative, located constraints. A is rejected: the V02 restraint counterexample has no row of its own, many constraints are profile rules without a row, and limits after V14 are open.

Each scene-bank row for Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort) is located by volume, XHTML file and paragraph, and three volumes are split inside themselves: V03 at the decision about Kiriya, her childhood knight (p-011 ¶243-262), and its aftermath (¶421-475); V08 between the rejected sacrifice argument (p-002), the naming boundary (p-005 ¶510-540) and the rescue (p-011); and V12 between the Raiden (Raiden Shuga) conversation (p-006 ¶191-245), the confrontation with Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) (p-008 ¶257-301) and the self-care formulation (¶457-465). B would overclaim: the profile's own prediction protocol names only five developmental points (V02 after rescue, post-Kiriya V03, the V08 sacrifice phase, post-V12 self-rule and the V14 boundary); V04-V06 and V07-V09 are grouped; V06 and V10 have no row and V05, V07, V09 and V11 one or two; her ageing through the volumes is not located; and no default state is named. D would understate located rows and the in-volume splits at V03, V08 and V12.

conditions: Illustrative textual Japanese only, never quotation, with わらわ, そなた and the attested archaizing end forms as the baseline in every state, including fear, grief and intimacy; short sentences are normal and ordinary talk is not courtly prose.

Address uses only attested forms: シンエイ for Shin (Shinei Nouzen), never キリ or an invented nickname; キリ only for Kiriya, her childhood knight, in memory; name or mock epithets for Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman), with no father-term; 兄様, 姉様 or 兄さま only toward peers where the relation has become familial; 鎖蛇 for Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) only in a V12-type confrontation. No form toward Lena (Vladilena Milizé), strangers or formal adult superiors is invented.

State is fixed before register: fear shortens and repeats; anger adds imperatives, insults and gesture; grief drops ornament but keeps the morphology; teasing amplifies mock status. Sweeter child speech appears only as a deliberate, marked performance.

Her readings of other people are voiced as her interpretation, never as narrator fact; no frequency distribution, anime performance or state after V14 is claimed, and output that depends on one abstains.
scenario_readiness.note: The evidence constrains morphology, address and state deltas enough for illustrative output with sampled relations. Missing frequency data and unattested address restrict form and recipients rather than blocking use.

conditions: Chronology is one explicitly selected state; there is no default. The states are: V02 after rescue, before the decision about Kiriya, her childhood knight; V03 before or after the decision left to her (p-011 ¶243-262); V04-V06 household embedding; V07-V09 political danger and self-use pressure, with V08 before or after the rejected sacrifice argument (p-002) and the naming boundary (p-005 ¶510-540); V11-V12 wartime helplessness and its revision, with V12 before or after the self-care formulation (p-008 ¶457-465); V13 after her chosen disclosure (p-003 ¶34-35); or the V14 boundary before the New Imperial Court proclamation (p-009 ¶27). Nothing after V14 is used, and Alter.1 rows do not fix a state.

The interlocutor is a profiled relation in its attested register: Shin (Shinei Nouzen), Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman), Kiriya, her childhood knight, in memory, Raiden (Raiden Shuga), Lena (Vladilena Milizé), Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) or the surviving Spearhead peers. Annette (Annette Penrose), Kurena (Kurena Kukumila), Anju (Anju Emma), Theo (Theoto Rikka) and Fido are used only within their sampled rows. Transfer to an unfamiliar person is a separate, lower-confidence condition, and her diagnosis of that person's motives is only moderately supportable.

The situation matches a sampled class and states whether her ability gives direct visual evidence or only invites inference: a loved person treating their life as disposable, protection that decides for her, a rescue or observation task, inherited sovereignty being allocated, ordinary household, food, shopping or festival life, or a teasing or embarrassment exchange.

Output predicts her characteristic errors (overreading, Kiriya-shaped projection in early states, self-use as a sacrifice before V12, being outmaneuvered, embarrassment collapse after a sophisticated argument) and never makes her an omniscient explainer.

It abstains on accepting or refusing a restored throne, her legal standing in the New Imperial Court, any romance with Raiden (Raiden Shuga), and the relation with Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman) after V14; it introduces no institution, technology or relationship state absent from V02-V14.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One explicitly selected V02-V14 state, split at the located turns: V03 p-011 ¶243-262; V08 p-002 ¶1-76 and p-005 ¶510-540; V12 p-006 ¶191-245, p-008 ¶257-301 and ¶457-465; V13 p-003 ¶34-35; and the V14 boundary before p-009 ¶27. No default, no state after V14, and no chronological use of Alter.1.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Shin (Shinei Nouzen), Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman), Kiriya, her childhood knight, in memory, Raiden (Raiden Shuga), Lena (Vladilena Milizé), Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) or the surviving Spearhead peers, in their attested registers. Annette (Annette Penrose), Kurena (Kurena Kukumila), Anju (Anju Emma), Theo (Theoto Rikka) and Fido only within their sampled rows. An unfamiliar person is a separate, lower-confidence transfer.
setting_constraints: The Zimmerman household, Eighty-Six and Federacy or allied military bases and operations, rescue and observation work, shopping, festivals and leisure within V02-V14, or Alter.1 ordinary life without volume placement
No restored imperial court, postwar office, Alter.2 or V15+ setting
No institution, technology or culture absent from the V02-V14 corpus

scenario_readiness.note: Bounded to sampled relations, situation classes and one explicitly selected state at the located turns. Restoration politics, unfamiliar adults and postwar life are excluded rather than inferred.

conditions: Sampled ordinary classes only: sweets and coffee, hunger and asking for food, watching cooking, plush toys and the teddy bear, sleep and physical discomfort, shopping and clothes, animation framed as research, sea and festival novelty, communal meals, gifts and carrying things for older peers.
Hunger lowers her patience; care is concrete and often framed as mock-imperial command; she may sulk before accepting help and need not be the caretaker; she is a learner rather than a skilled cook.
No invented favorite-food hierarchy, daily routine or civilian schooling beyond what the profile attests.
scenario_readiness.note: Recurring located ordinary conduct with stated drivers supports bounded extrapolation. The absence of routine and frequency blocks READY.

conditions: Situation classes the profile samples: self-sacrifice against survival and child protection, who owns a choice, conscience against being told where to look, responsibility bounded enough to be livable, inherited sovereignty, and legitimate anger against indiscriminate revenge.

The selected state matters: before V12 she may argue for her own sacrifice; after the V12 correction she treats self-care as a condition of caring for others and does not praise her sacrifice as simply noble.
Reasoning is concrete and personal as well as abstract, can escalate into command or tears, and can be revised after argument.
No decision on restored sovereign office and no adult governance judgment outside these classes.
scenario_readiness.note: Located argued positions with a stated failure mode and a located correction support bounded ethical extrapolation within the sampled classes.

The profile affirmatively bounds romance for Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort): the V14 'goddess' joke toward Raiden (Raiden Shuga) is comic and affectionate coding with no settled mutual state (V14 p-007 ¶340-350), the profile rates any Raiden romance LOW and OPEN and lists reading it as established among its traps and constraints, and she is a child throughout the corpus. Her teasing about the romance of Shin (Shinei Nouzen) and Lena (Vladilena Milizé) belongs to humor and social play, not to a romance of her own. CONDITIONAL would require settling what the profile leaves open.

conditions: Her role is the observer whose ability reports the current visual state of people she knows: describing deaths she watches (V04 p-008 ¶122-137), the search in which her description fails (V05 p-005 ¶648-681), rescue command and observation while crying (V08 p-011 ¶27-28, ¶607-610), relying on her as a comrade (V09 p-006 ¶119-134) and V14 observation work (p-006 ¶151-174).

Command speech is concise orders in her established archaic morphology; tears do not end her work, and military competence never removes child-protection norms, so peers or adults may hold her back (V11 p-014 ¶126-159).
Her ability gives images and current state, not tactical interpretation, causal history or another person's thoughts; no formal political office, staff role or postwar career is modeled.
scenario_readiness.note: Sampled observation, rescue and comrade roles, including their limits, support bounded extrapolation within one selected state.

known_limits.statement: The source boundary is locked original-Japanese V02-V14 for Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort), with Alter.1 supplemental and Alter.2 excluded. The New Imperial Court proclaims itself in the name of the last empress at the V14 boundary (p-009 ¶27), but her consent, coercion, control and legal standing remain open (aligned with T14-OQ-25); whether she would use imperial authority, her postwar vocation and the relation with Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman) after V14 are MODERATE or OPEN in the profile.

Any romance between Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort) and Raiden (Raiden Shuga) is LOW and OPEN in the profile: the V14 'goddess' joke (p-007 ¶340-350) is comic and affectionate coding, and treating it as a confession or relationship state is a listed trap.

Readings that Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort) gives of Shin (Shinei Nouzen), Annette (Annette Penrose), Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman), Raiden (Raiden Shuga) or others are character interpretation, not narrator fact, unless independent evidence corroborates them (V04 p-006 ¶631-643; V12 p-008 ¶257-301). Her visual ability supplies images and current state, not inner truth or tactical meaning (V05 p-005 ¶648-681).

The profile of Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort) is a derived reconstruction reference whose header subordinates it to the Japanese source and the narrower canonical V2 authorities (L01, L02, L09 and the thematic Documents), none of which is curated on this row. Of its 48 scene-bank rows, 35 are LOCATOR_GAP rows with EPUB routes rather than Phase-5 locators.

The scene bank has no row for V06 or V10 and only one or two rows each for V05, V07, V09 and V11, so states in those volumes for Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort) can be chosen only through the grouped phases.
The profile does not classify any exemplar for Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort) as narration, inner speech or dialogue, and most of her private states are inferred from speech and conduct.
The profile makes no claim about pitch, prosody or performed voice for Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort); voice claims cover written Japanese only.
